subject: Re: Security questionnaire — data residency, retention & deletion (hosted API)
messages:
From: Anne Martin <anne.martin@helixfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@helixfin.com
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security questionnaire: data residency and deletion — Redwood hosted API

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for agreeing to take our questionnaire. We need definitive, audit-ready answers for the hosted API usage model for an internal review and to present to procurement. High-level asks below — we prefer concise, numbered responses we can paste into our security spreadsheet.

1) Where does customer data (API request/response payloads, logs, embeddings) physically reside for hosted API customers? Which cloud regions and providers are used?
2) What is the default retention period for: (a) request/response payloads (for debugging), (b) embeddings & vector indices, (c) operational logs, and (d) backups/snapshots?
3) Describe the deletion/erasure workflow. If Helix requests full erasure for a tenant, what steps does Redwood take and what timelines can we expect?
4) How do you handle backups, snapshots, and disaster-recovery copies during an erasure request? Are backups re-identified or purged?
5) What proof/evidence can you provide once deletion is complete?
6) Do you support regional data residency controls for hosted API customers (i.e., restrict storage to a specific geography)? If so, which regions and how is it enforced?
7) Are there exceptions (legal hold, logs for billing, fraud detection) where data may be retained beyond requested deletion?

We attached our template security spreadsheet. Can you reply by EOD PT Tuesday 2027-05-04? If any of the above needs a short follow-up call, happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Anne Martin
Head of Security Operations
Helix Financial

Attachment: helix_security_qna_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anne Martin <anne.martin@helixfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: data residency and deletion — Redwood hosted API

Anne — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, audit-ready answers; I attached a formal playbook and a retention matrix that maps data classes to retention and deletion procedures. If you want any items redlined into your template, we can paste them directly.

Summary answers (hosted API):

1) Physical location of data
- Primary: AWS us-west-2 and us-east-1 (default per-customer region routing).
- Secondary (disaster recovery/replication): GCP us-central1 for select customers with explicit contractual requests.
- Note: For customers requiring strict geo residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private; hosted API supports region pinning where available — see Q6.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API, default configuration unless altered via account settings or contract):
- a) Request/response payloads (debug traces): 30 days from ingestion (rolling window). Shorter windows available via customer settings; retention can be reduced to 7 days by request prior to contract signature.
- b) Embeddings & vector indices: 90 days by default for hosted indexing features; embeddings persisted only if customer opts into the embedding store. Ephemeral embedding cache used for inference is 24 hours.
- c) Operational logs (service logs, API access logs): 90 days for metrics/observability. Audit logs (who-accessed-what) retained for 365 days by default for production accounts.
- d) Backups/snapshots: incremental snapshots (for DR) retained 35 days on average; full-image snapshots retained 90 days in our standard retention policy.

3) Deletion / erasure workflow (tenant-level erasure):
- Step 1: Customer submits an erasure request via the Console or our compliance mailbox (compliance@redwood.com).
- Step 2: We verify authority and scope (24 hours).
- Step 3: Initiate live-data purge across primary storage (S3/GCS) — live objects removed within 48 hours.
- Step 4: Invalidate/expire caches and in-memory KV entries (immediate).
- Step 5: Schedule deletion from backups/snapshots — background purge process with target completion within 30 days; customers receive a completion report.
- Step 6: Update audit record and provide deletion manifest.
- Total timeline: live data removal within 48 hours; full deletion including backups within 30 calendar days barring legal hold.

4) Backups & snapshots during erasure
- Backups are logically tagged by tenant identifier. On an erasure request, we mark backup objects for deletion and initiate background purge jobs. Due to immutable snapshot mechanics and replication, final deletion from cold/archival tiers can take up to 30 days. We provide a manifest of objects removed and S3/GCS object IDs where applicable.

5) Proof / evidence provided
- Deletion manifest (list of object keys removed), signed by Redwood Compliance (PDF).
- S3/GCS lifecycle reports and job IDs for purge operations (redacted where needed).
- For higher-assurance needs we can provide a snapshot of our audit log entries showing the erase workflow steps and timestamps.

6) Regional residency controls (hosted API)
- We support region pinning for hosted API customers in: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1 (EU customers). Support for APAC regions is available on request.
- Enforcement: control plane enforces storage region for persistent artifacts; inference routing ensures primary compute + storage are colocated in the pinned region where capacity allows. Customers may opt for Dedicated/Private for strict single-region guarantees.

7) Exceptions & legal hold
- Legal holds: if Helix notifies Redwood of a legal hold (with appropriate authority), we suspend erasure and retain affected data until released.
- Required retention: minimal billing metadata (transaction ids, billing invoice records) may be preserved for up to 3 years for accounting and fraud investigations; we scope this narrowly and provide extracts on request.

Additional operational notes:
- Encryption: all persistent data encrypted at rest with customer-project keys in KMS-managed envelopes. Key rotation does not prevent deletion.
- Search & indices: embedding indices are rekeyed and trimmed as part of the purge; we can provide index prune manifests.
- PII redaction: Redwood does not perform PII redaction by default; we provide tools for customers to submit redaction patterns.

Attachments included: Redwood_Retention_Playbook_v1.pdf (playbook), Retention_Matrix_v2.xlsx (data-class matrix).

If you want, Monica (cc'd) can join a short call to walk through the manifest examples. Happy to paste the above into your spreadsheet format if that helps.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Retention_Playbook_v1.pdf (PDF stub), Retention_Matrix_v2.xlsx (Excel stub)

Soojin — thank you, this is very helpful and sufficient for our initial review. A couple quick clarifications before we close the item: 1) Can you confirm the 30-day backup purge applies to encrypted archival tiers as well? 2) For the deletion manifest format, can you provide a sample (anonymized) so we can validate it against our evidence checklist?

If those two items are available, procurement can move forward.

Anne
